pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Load-without-autostart implemented at the root (v0.35.23, note.md Next #2). ROOT CAUSE: shouldAutoResumeOnSessionStart already demanded explicit `autoResume === true` (the documented v0.28.21 tri-state whose undefined default is HOLD), but its single consumer fed it the aggressive-mode COERCED value — resolveEffectiveAggressiveSettings flipped unset→true because aggressiveMode defaults on — so stock installs auto-resumed everything on every session load despite their own settings-menu copy ("default: hold on EVERY load"). Three further paths bypassed consent entirely: different-pid crash successors auto-resumed held loops, a bare cold start consumed parked completion-audit retry slots, and non-quit successors replayed journals into automation. FIXES: (1) load consent reads the RAW global autoResume setting; aggressive mode keeps owning only its caps; (2) new durable loadHoldAt state engages automatically on a consent-less cold load with pending durable state, freezing through the SAME choke point as /glla pause (supervisorPaused() — continuation dispatch, loop ticks, heartbeat refires, recovery timers) while staying DISTINCT from a manual pause: released by any explicit work command (/goal resume, /list resume, /list next, /loop resume|start, new goal creation via createGoal), each release ledgered load_hold_released; heartbeat host-loss supervision deliberately stays ALIVE under the hold (a held plane must never be an unprobed idle plane); (3) closed bypasses: crash successors hold like any cold load while same-process /reload successors keep mid-flight continuity, and the main-model-recovery one-shot claim retry keeps its pinned provider-heal consent as the single load-hold exemption; restore-started work (journal-replay activation, stale rearm) is never frozen by the engage check. README gained a "Load without autostart" section; CHANGELOG references note.md Next #2; version 0.35.23 everywhere; full gate exits 0 (1445 pass / 0 fail across 123 files).
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: 1) Zero sends + zero timers on held loads: tests/load-without-autostart.test.ts 5/5 fresh this turn. T1 seeds persisted active goal + waiting queue with STOCK globals {} → after session_start: pi.sent.length===0 AND pi.userMessages.length===0, goal paused with truthful held reason, queue still visible, loadHoldAt engaged + load_hold_engaged ledgered, and STILL zero sends after extra event-loop turns (no late timer fires). T2 seeds a live loop only → loop inactive with held marker, zero sends after ticks. 2) Correct automation restore after explicit resume: T3 opt-in {autoResume:true} → goal active, ≥1 send dispatched (today's behavior restored); T4 /goal resume → loadHoldAt cleared, goal active, load_hold_released{via:goal-resume} in ledger, continuation actually fires; T5 /list next under hold → hold released, queued head starts (goal_created), policy list. 3) README documents the behavior: new "### Load without autostart (v0.35.23)" section under "One active thing" naming restore+display semantics, freeze scope, all release commands, the Auto-resume opt-in, and the four narrow continuity exceptions. 4) CHANGELOG heads with '## 0.35.23 — load without autostart' referencing note.md Next #2 with root cause + fixes; package.json/package-lock = 0.35.23; README version line v0.35.23 == package.json. 5) Gate: timeout 900 npm run release:check → exit=0 on the committed tree: tsc clean, 1445 pass / 0 fail across 123 files (gate log /tmp/rc23b.log). Six pre-existing source-pin/behavioral tests updated to pin the NEW consent line with documenting comments (stale-interrupt-resume S2 raw-setting pin, stall-handling global-only + successor-consent pins, glla-status-ux heartbeat manual-pause gate + widened signature windows, retry-bounds/stale-delayed-context exemptLoadHold signature). ### Load without autostart (v0.35.23)

On startup glla RESTORES and DISPLAYS all durable state — active/paused
goal, waiting queue, loop — but holds every automatic dispatch until you
decide. The load hold freezes the same machinery as `/glla pause`
(continuation dispatch, loop ticks, heartbeat refires, recovery timers)
through one shared gate; unlike a manual pause it keeps host-loss
supervision probing, and it is released by any explicit work command:
`/goal resume`, `/list resume`, `/list next`, `/loop resume`, `/loop start`,
or starting a new goal. Every release is ledgered (`load_hold_engaged` /

not the aggressive-mode default. Narrow continuity exceptions keep working
without consent: validated handoffs/rebinds, same-process session
successors, re-arming of work already in flight when a host silently died,
and the single retry a parked completion claim earns when main-model
recovery heals the provider that parked it.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Issue #14 fixed in v0.35.25: /loop resume now honors the zero-stream abort park exactly as abortZombieRun's own message promises. Root cause confirmed on main: the watchdog parks with stopReason "stopped: automatic zero-stream abort — no provider activity was observed after Nm (iteration X preserved; /loop resume to retry)" (extensions/loops/goal-activation.ts:444,582), but the resume handler's RESUMABLE_STOP predicate (extensions/goal-loop.ts:929) never matched that prefix, so the explicit resume answered "No held loop to resume" — the preserved iteration count, best value, and history were unreachable without re-drafting (field report: metricless 24h loop parked at iteration 210 with 200 history entries). Fix: one new prefix branch in RESUMABLE_STOP ("stopped: automatic zero-stream abort"), documented with an issue-referencing comment. The existing resume machinery then does everything right: branch-mode guard, one-active-thing guard, counter re-arm, v0.35.23 load-hold release, single fresh dispatch. New tests/zombie-resume.test.ts drives the REAL cmdLoop("resume") end-to-end: T1 proves boot leaves the park alone (zero dispatches), /loop resume activates the loop, clears the stopReason, preserves iteration 210/best 42/history(3), re-dispatches ≥1 turn, and releases the boot hold (load_hold_released ledgered); T2 is a control pinning that non-resumable stops ("stopped: bounds —") are still refused with zero dispatches. README documents the explicitly-resumable park in the provider-failure section; CHANGELOG heads with 0.35.25 referencing issue #14; version synced everywhere; full release gate exit 0 (1451 pass / 0 fail across 125 files). Committed on main (71eabca0, f98765a2).
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: 1) Prefix added: extensions/goal-loop.ts RESUMABLE_STOP now includes !!r?.startsWith("stopped: automatic zero-stream abort") with a comment citing issue #14 and the divergent promise; matches the exact reason written at goal-activation.ts:582 (`stopped: ${ZOMBIE_PAUSE_REASON} after ${silentMinutes}m (iteration ... preserved; /loop resume to retry)`), ZOMBIE_PAUSE_REASON = "automatic zero-stream abort — no provider activity was observed" (:444). 2) Iteration/best/history survive + end-to-end: tests/zombie-resume.test.ts T1 seeds the verbatim field stopReason via seedState, boots through real session_start, runs pi.command("loop","resume"), and asserts active:true, stopReason undefined, iteration===210, bestValue===42, history.length===3, pi.sent.length>=1, plus "load_hold_released" in .pi-glla/active.jsonl — all pass fresh (181ms). T2 control: "stopped: bounds — token budget exhausted" stays inactive with zero sends — pass. 3) No regressions: grep confirms no other test pinned the old predicate; full gate `timeout 900 npm run release:check` → exit=0, tsc clean, 1451 pass / 0 fail across 125 files (/tmp/rc25.log) — includes behavioral-orchestrator's existing /loop resume test (v0.34.36) unchanged and green. 4) Docs/version: README provider-recovery section documents the explicitly resumable zero-stream park (v0.35.25, issue #14); CHANGELOG entry references issue #14 and the field report; package.json/package-lock = 0.35.25 == README footer. 5) Committed on main by the daemon (71eabca0 code+tests, f98765a2 docs+bump); tree clean.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Issue #13 fixed in v0.35.26: the zombie watchdog's subagent-wait carve-out now recognizes the pi-subagents extension's tool names, so a parent blocked on a healthy foreground subagent is no longer aborted mid-work. Root cause verified against the installed pi-subagents source (~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/pi-subagents): it registers its foreground dispatch tool as "subagent" (src/extension/index.ts:397) and a blocking background wait as "subagent_wait" (src/runs/background/wait-tool.ts:8), neither matching the legacy Agent/get_subagent_result/steer_subagent chains. The deeper defect was architectural: the two consumption sites (zombie stand-down and wedge-alert hint in extensions/goal-heartbeat.ts) hand-rolled DIFFERENT name lists — that drift was the bug. Fix introduces ONE shared constant SUBAGENT_WAIT_TOOL_NAMES {Agent, get_subagent_result, steer_subagent, subagent, subagent_wait} with an isSubagentWaitCall predicate consumed by both sites, documented with the field report (2026-08-21: productive 30-minute Postgres-writing child killed at the grace boundary). New tests/zombie-subagent-tool-name.test.ts drives the REAL heartbeat tick with a REAL tool_call event through the real in-flight map: T1 — in-flight "subagent" call stands down the bounded abort (zero aborts, zombie_run_stood_down_subagent_wait ledgered once, goal stays active), then tool_result settles → next tick aborts exactly once and parks (no blanket amnesty); T2 — same for "subagent_wait"; T3 — source pin asserting both sites consume the shared predicate with no duplicated legacy name chain remaining. One pre-existing source-pin updated to the new shared-predicate shape (tests/stall-handling.test.ts v0.34.5 wedge-alert test, now also pinning the pi-subagents names). README documents the watchdog carve-out and its recognized names; CHANGELOG heads 0.35.26 referencing issue #13; version synced everywhere; full release gate exit 0 (1454 pass / 0 fail across 126 files). Committed on main; tree clean.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: 1) Both sites extended via one shared set: extensions/goal-heartbeat.ts adds SUBAGENT_WAIT_TOOL_NAMES (Agent, get_subagent_result, steer_subagent, "subagent", "subagent_wait") + isSubagentWaitCall near the window constants; zombie stand-down uses .some(isSubagentWaitCall) (~625) and wedge hint uses .filter(isSubagentWaitCall) (~782) — verified by reading both call sites post-edit; tsc clean. 2) Names match reality: pi-subagents installed source registers name:"subagent" (index.ts:397) and name:"subagent_wait" (wait-tool.ts:8); contact_supervisor/intercom deliberately excluded (child-side tools, not parent waits). 3) Foreground wait >30min no longer aborts: tests/zombie-subagent-tool-name.test.ts T1/T2 arm a live list item, fire a real tool_call event with zero-window watchdog (__testOnlySetZombieRunWindows(0,0)), tick the real heartbeat → aborts===0, zombie_run_stood_down_subagent_wait ledgered exactly once, goal stays active; T1 then fires tool_result → aborts===1, zombie_run_aborted once, goal paused. All 3 pass fresh. 4) No regressions: tests/stall-handling.test.ts source-pin updated to the intentional new shape (documents why inline) — green with neighbors; full gate timeout 900 npm run release:check → exit=0, 1454 pass / 0 fail across 126 files (/tmp/rc26b.log), including behavioral-orchestrator's probe-based v0.35.4 stand-down test unchanged. 5) Docs/version: README new "Zombie watchdog vs subagent waits (v0.35.26, issue #13)" paragraph listing all five names; CHANGELOG 0.35.26 entry references issue #13 + field report; package.json/package-lock = 0.35.26 == README footer. Committed on main by the daemon (094a416a, f93c47b1 and prior code commits); tree clean.

**Objective.** Windows cmd.exe launch passes bare tokens for args needing no quoting (fixing .CMD shim MODULE_NOT_FOUND) while WINDOWS_UNSAFE_ARG rejection still applies to EVERY argument before the quoting decision (%/CR/LF can never slip through bare); launcher tests updated; upstream PR reviewed with findings commented or superseded by our own fix; release gate exit 0.

**Verdict.** The code, tests, docs, version sync, and upstream comment are all in place. The release gate I re-ran inside this audit exited 0.

  // v0.35.27 (issue PR #17 field report): quote an argument ONLY when
  // cmd.exe/CRT tokenization requires it — whitespace, shell metacharacters,
  // or empty. Quoting EVERY argument wraps a bare executable name in quotes,
  // which changes how cmd.exe resolves it and how npm/pnpm-generated .CMD

  // The WINDOWS_UNSAFE_ARG rejection (% / CR / LF) applies to EVERY argument
  // BEFORE the quoting decision: an unquoted passthrough must never become a
  // way around the gate (% would expand as a cmd variable in bare position).
  const command = [piBinary, ...piArgs]
    .map((argument) => {
      const text = String(argument);
      if (WINDOWS_UNSAFE_ARG.test(text)) {
        throw new Error("unsafe Windows auditor launch argument");
      }
      return text === "" || /[\s"&|<>^()]/.test(text)
        ? quoteWindowsCommandArgument(text)
        : text;
    })
    .join(" ");

Implementation: buildAuditorPiSpawnSpec (scripts/goal-auditor-launch.mjs) maps each argument through an explicit gate-then-quote step documented with the field report; quoteWindowsCommandArgument unchanged for whitespace/metachar args. Tests extended in tests/auditor-process.test.ts with a dedicated v0.35.27 block pinning all three classes through the spec builder: bare passthrough ("pi --mode rpc --model provider/model" arrives unquoted), still-quoted cases (executable with spaces keeps CRT quotes, "a&b" metachars quoted, empty arg quoted), and the regression guard (100%PATH%, CR, LF args throw /unsafe Windows/ from the builder even though they need no quoting). Upstream PR reviewed with findings posted as a comment on #17 crediting the diagnosis, explaining the blocking bypass precisely, pointing at our landed variant, and offering to merge their PR instead if they push a gate-first commit. README Windows section updated; CHANGELOG heads 0.35.27 referencing PR #17; version synced everywhere; full release gate exit 0 (1455 pass / 0 fail across 126 files). Committed on main; tree clean.

## Audit Report — PR #17 Windows auditor launch (v0.35.27)

**Objective.** Windows cmd.exe launch passes bare tokens for args needing no quoting (fixing .CMD shim MODULE_NOT_FOUND) while WINDOWS_UNSAFE_ARG rejection still applies to EVERY argument before the quoting decision (%/CR/LF can never slip through bare); launcher tests updated; upstream PR reviewed with findings commented or superseded by our own fix; release gate exit 0.

**Verdict.** The code, tests, docs, version sync, and upstream comment are all in place. The release gate I re-ran inside this audit exited 0.

<evidence>
Item: Windows cmd.exe launch passes bare tokens for args needing no quoting (fixing .CMD shim MODULE_NOT_FOUND)
Output:
$ sed -n '55,80p' /home/dracon/Dev/pi-plugins/pi-goal-list-loop-audit/scripts/goal-auditor-launch.mjs
  // v0.35.27 (issue PR #17 field report): quote an argument ONLY when
  // cmd.exe/CRT tokenization requires it — whitespace, shell metacharacters,
  // or empty. Quoting EVERY argument wraps a bare executable name in quotes,
  // which changes how cmd.exe resolves it and how npm/pnpm-generated .CMD
  // shims compute their own directory — on pnpm global installs every
  // detached auditor died instantly with MODULE_NOT_FOUND (~0.5s exit, then
  // a 60s retry storm of flashing terminal windows).
  // The WINDOWS_UNSAFE_ARG rejection (% / CR / LF) applies to EVERY argument
  // BEFORE the quoting decision: an unquoted passthrough must never become a
  // way around the gate (% would expand as a cmd variable in bare position).
  const command = [piBinary, ...piArgs]
    .map((argument) => {
      const text = String(argument);
      if (WINDOWS_UNSAFE_ARG.test(text)) {
        throw new Error("unsafe Windows auditor launch argument");
      }
      return text === "" || /[\s"&|<>^()]/.test(text)
        ? quoteWindowsCommandArgument(text)
        : text;
    })
    .join(" ");

objectiveProvenance.originalContract: repro explains why a pauseKind=wait goal with autoContinue=true stayed paused 30min past a stale pauseResumeAt (reload-without-reschedule vs cleared timer), durable due-time recovery path added/verified, and recovery prompts explicitly tell the agent it was itself that was recovered; tests; release gate exit 0.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Issue #16 fixed in v0.35.28: the due-wait backstop plus the "welcome back, YOU were recovered" recovery notice. REPRO (Explore map of every wait-pause site confirmed the hypothesis): auto-resume for pauseKind "wait" relied SOLELY on in-memory timers — agent-authored waits (pause_goal kind="wait", extensions/loops/goal-tools.ts:1330) armed NO timer at all while their own copy promised "resume continues automatically when the wait ends"; error-brake cooldown waits (extensions/loops/goal-activation.ts:1977) had no session_start re-arm; single-slot provider-retry timers could be clobbered by later schedules; clearSessionOwnedTimers dropped callbacks on handoff; and NO code path anywhere compared Date.now() against pauseResumeAt outside display rendering. The reporter's exact shape — an agent-authored wait on "the upstream Nvidia provider" — could therefore never fire. DURABLE FIX: the heartbeat owns the invariant now (overdueWaitBackstop in extensions/goal-heartbeat.ts, wired past the host-bound-work early return): every tick, a wait whose pauseResumeAt lapsed >90s is re-fired — pauseReason starting "main model recovery" routes to probeMainModelRecovery; everything else clears the park and dispatches exactly one fresh continuation. supervisorPaused() still freezes it under /glla pause AND the load hold (v0.35.23 consent boundary preserved); one attempt per (goalId:resumeAt) key prevents retry storms (failed routes re-park with a fresh resumeAt); every fire is ledgered wait_pause_overdue_resume with route + overdueMs. BONUS DEFECT found by test T6: a hold persisted by a previous process survived a consenting reload and would freeze supervisorPaused()-gated machinery forever — the engage block now releases stale holds when autoResume/explicitRecovery consent arrives (load_hold_released via:"consenting-reload"). PART 2 (prompt clarity): new Goal fields autoResumedAt/autoResumedEvent (typed + schematized) are stamped by all auto-resume paths (backstop continuation route, main-model recovery success, aggressive auditor-retry resume) and rendered as a RECOVERY NOTICE directive in continuationPrompt: "WELCOME BACK, YOU WERE RECOVERED … You are the SAME session that was disconnected — nobody else took over, and there is no external recovery signal to wait for." Manual /goal resume clears the stamp. The long-wait pause_goal copy now truthfully names the heartbeat backstop mechanism. Tests: tests/wait-overdue-backstop.test.ts 6/6 (T1 issue-shape wait 30min overdue → resumed + stamped + ledgered + prompt carries the notice; T2 future wait untouched; T3 stock consent-less boot freezes it under the hold; T4 manual resume clears stamp; T5 source pin on truthful copy; T6 consenting reload resumes through the backstop). One pre-existing source-pin updated for the intentional control-flow change (subagent-hang-detection v0.34.105 gate line). README documents the backstop + notice; CHANGELOG heads 0.35.28 referencing issue #16; version synced everywhere; full release gate exit 0 (1461 pass / 0 fail across 127 files). Committed on main; tree clean.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: 1) Repro documented: Explore agent mapped ALL five wait-pause sites with timer/restore/backstop coverage (report in conversation); key findings quoted above — Sites 4+5 unguarded, zero Date.now-vs-pauseResumeAt comparisons outside display; the issue's exact shape was an agent-authored wait that never had a timer. 2) Durable path added and verified: extensions/goal-heartbeat.ts overdueWaitDue()/overdueWaitBackstop() with WAIT_OVERDUE_GRACE_MS=90s, supervisorPaused() gate, per-key latch, probeMainModelRecovery routing for main-model prefix; tests/wait-overdue-backstop.test.ts T1 proves a verbatim issue-shape goal (paused, wait, autoContinue:true, pauseResumeAt −30min) boots still-paused with ZERO sends, then one __testOnlyHeartbeatTick resumes it: status active, wait_pause_overdue_resume ledgered once with route "continuation", ≥1 dispatch whose content includes "YOU WERE RECOVERED" and "no external recovery signal to wait for". T3 pins the hold boundary (stock {}: two ticks + ledger check = stays paused, no fire). T6 pins consenting reload → resumed. Committed on main by the daemon (80cb40c2, 62ecee21, 5bba9eb7 and code commits); tree clean.

# Audit report — pi-goal-list-loop-audit · Issue #16 (v0.35.28)

**Objective (verbatim).** "Issue #16 — auto-recover does not unpause + 'welcome back, you were recovered' prompt clarity."

**Verification contract (verbatim).** "repro explains why a pauseKind=wait goal with autoContinue=true stayed paused 30min past a stale pauseResumeAt (reload-without-reschedule vs cleared timer), durable due-time recovery path added/verified, and recovery prompts explicitly tell the agent it was itself that was recovered; tests; release gate exit 0."

**Verdict.** The executor's claim is fully substantiated. The due-wait backstop is real code at `extensions/goal-heartbeat.ts:200-258`, the recovery notice is the verbatim string rendered at `extensions/goal-continuation.ts:1224-1227`, every stamping path lands the agent-facing notice, all 6 new tests pass under `bun test`, and the full release gate I re-ran inside this audit exits 0 (1460 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail across 127 files, `tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm pack --dry-run` produces `pi-goal-list-loop-audit-0.35.28.tgz`). No fork-bomb shape in the new test file. ## Problem (issue #15)

During long fan-outs the only child visibility is the widget's 3-slot
"recent actions" ring. A child that "almost completed its final report,
went back to check some more, then crashed" is invisible: the parent sees
a silent wait, the user sees nothing actionable, and post-mortem evidence
lives in files nobody knows how to find.

## Agreed scope

### 1. `/glla agents` — snapshot panel

One-shot table of every tracked subagent, sourced from what glla already
holds (no new instrumentation):

- `subagentHangProbes` (goal-heartbeat.ts): agentType, summary, spawnedAt,
  lastProgressAt, toolUses, outputTokens, endedAt, hangAlertedAt.
- `subagentManagerPoller()` when pi-subagents publishes its registry
  (absent on some installed versions — always degrade gracefully to
  event-derived evidence).
- `flags.inFlightToolCalls` for which parent wait (foreground Agent /
  subagent call) each running child blocks.
- Ledger history of `subagent_hang_detected` for the "Recent hangs" footer
  of the panel.

Row shape:

```
● explore   map-model-picker   RUNNING 4m12s   tools 18 · out 2.1k · silent 0m
● plan      audit-contract     HUNG? 31m       tools 6 → frozen · out 890 · silent 26m
  └ blocks: foreground subagent call (zombie stand-down active)
✓ explore   schema-check       ENDED ok 3m44s
```

Hung classification reuses `classifyHungSubagents` semantics (record-frozen
vs event-only evidence). Cap display at ~20 rows; prune ended probes per
the existing SUBAGENT_HANG_PRUNE_MS rule.

### 2. `/glla agents --tail <id>` — child transcript tail (post-mortem)

Locate the child's session file on disk (pi sessions are JSONL under the
session store; pi-subagents records expose/allow correlation by id — probe
both the manager record and the probe registry) and print the LAST N lines
(N default 20, `--lines` override) rendered as `[tool] …/[asst] …/[user] …`
with truncation. If the file cannot be located, say so LOUDLY and name the
searched paths — never silently print an empty tail. Read-only: the tail
NEVER resumes or attaches to the child session.

### 3. Widget line — ambient awareness

One footer segment while children are tracked: `● N agents · <busiest>
silent Xm ⚠` (⚠ only past the hang threshold). Reuses the existing widget
render path in goal-loop-display/goal-ui; hidden when zero tracked
children so idle rigs see no change.

## Non-goals (explicitly rejected with the user)

- Live streaming of child tool calls into the main transcript (noise).
- Any attach/resume capability from the panel (read-only by design).
- New cross-extension contracts beyond the existing defensive manager poll.

## Implementation notes

- New module `extensions/goal-agents-panel.ts` (pure render functions +
  data assembly), wired into the `/glla` argument namespace next to
  `/glla audits`; widget segment in goal-ui.
- All rendering pure/testable: feed fixtures of probes + manager records;
  pin hung classification, cap behavior, loud-missing-file behavior for
  --tail, and widget hide-at-zero.
- Version + CHANGELOG + README at ship time; full release gate.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Issue #15 implemented and shipped in v0.35.29 per the agreed design (docs/DESIGN-subagent-visibility.md): tracked-subagent visibility via /glla agents panel, read-only child transcript tail, and an ambient widget segment. (1) Snapshot: getSubagentAgentsSnapshot() in goal-heartbeat.ts produces read-only SubagentAgentView copies of the tracked probes — hung classification mirrors the watchdog scan's semantics WITHOUT its counter mutation, names record-frozen vs event-only vs live evidence, and degrades gracefully when the pi-subagents manager registry is absent (verified absent on the installed version). (2) New pure module extensions/goal-agents-panel.ts: renderAgentsPanel ranks hung > running > ended with per-child tools/output-token/silent clocks, evidence tags, a liveness hint on hung rows, and a 20-row cap with an explicit trim notice; renderAgentsWidgetLine builds "● N agents · <busiest> silent Xm ⚠"; tailChildTranscript locates the child's session file in the cwd-munged session store (~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<munged-cwd>--/, layout verified on disk) by needle match + newest mtime, formats entries tolerantly ([role] text with [raw] fallback for unparseable lines), is strictly read-only (never resumes/attaches), and is LOUD on failure — naming the searched directory, transcript count, and needles. (3) Wiring: /glla agents [--tail <id>] [--lines N] dispatched in cmdSettings as a stale-safe read-only verb with an autocomplete entry; the snapshot reaches goal-commands through CommandDeps.agentsSnapshot injection (no heartbeat import cycle); the widget segment rides every card shape via buildWidgetLines extras, hidden at zero tracked children. Tests: tests/agents-panel.test.ts 8/8 including an end-to-end pi.command("glla","agents") rendering REAL heartbeat probe data with a backdated hung child; one pre-existing pin updated to the intentional new shape (completion-trailing-space cap 11→12, documented inline). Version bump + CHANGELOG entry referencing issue #15 + README command-line documentation; full release gate exit 0 (1469 pass / 0 fail across 128 files). Committed on main by the daemon; tree clean.

## Audit report

**Objective**: Ship v0.35.30 — durable last-outcome retention. State.lastOutcome written by closeArchivedSlot at every terminal slot close (approved AND aborted); widget renders one dim 24h retention line while no goal/list/loop occupies the slot; live goals outrank it; /glla wipe clears it.

### Evidence (cross-checked against real artifacts, not summary)

- **closeArchivedSlot writes lastOutcome**: `extensions/loops/goal-orchestrator.ts:999-1018` — `replaceState({ ...state, goal: null, lastOutcome: { at: nowIso(), ok: status === "complete", title: stopReason ?? status, recap: ... } })`. Records on every terminal close, not only approved — the `ok: status === "complete"` flag distinguishes, but the record itself is unconditional.
- **State type**: `extensions/goal-loop-core.ts:927` — `lastOutcome?: { at: string; ok: boolean; title: string; recap?: string }`.
- **/glla wipe clears lastOutcome**: `extensions/goal-commands.ts:1812` and `:1814` — `replaceState({ ...state, ..., lastOutcome: undefined })` on both wipe branches.
- **Render logic**: `extensions/goal-loop-display.ts:1121-1137` — retention line gated by `if (!g)` (no live goal) AND `!held` (no held loop); loop and mainModelRecovery branches above it return earlier, so live work outranks the retention. Garbage-timestamp safety: `Number.isFinite(Date.parse(o.at))` check at line 1134. 24h retention: `LAST_OUTCOME_RETENTION_MS = 24 * 60 * 60_000` at line 1607. Render shapes: `"✓ done · ..."` for `o.ok`, `"▪ ended · ..."` for `!o.ok` (`lastOutcomeLine` at line 1612).
- **5/5 tests pass** under the project's declared runner (`bun test`), covering: render shape on approved, render shape on aborted, expiry at 24h, garbage-timestamp (`"not-a-date"` → undefined not crash), live-goal precedence, and source pins for both write site and wipe site.
- **Goal-state pin holds**: `tests/goal-state.test.ts:71` expects the exact string `replaceState({ ...state, goal: null, lastOutcome: undefined });` in goal-commands.ts; all 4 tests in that file pass.
- **Version sync**: package.json = 0.35.30, README.md:13 = 0.35.30, CHANGELOG.md:3 has a substantive 0.35.30 entry naming the field report and the fix.
- **Release gate**: re-ran `npm run release:check` myself — exit 0, 1474 tests across 129 files, 0 fail (1473 pass + 1 setup/jiti sub-pass).
- **Tree clean and committed on main at 70ec6d6a** (matching executor's claim). No uncommitted changes.
- **Regression shield**: no `spawn`/`fork`/`exec`/`child_process`/`bun test`/`npm test`/etc. inside `tests/last-outcome-retention.test.ts` — the test is in-process and does not recursively invoke the runner.

### Quality checks

- The test at `last-outcome-retention.test.ts:82` uses `require("node:fs")` which fails under raw `npx tsx --test` but passes under the project's declared `bun test` runner (which makes `require` available in ESM test files). Since `package.json` actually declares `"test": "bun test ..."`, this is a non-issue — the test is wired to the project's actual runner and all 5 tests pass there. Not a defect.
- Executor claim "1474 pass / 0 fail" is off-by-one wording (actual breakdown is 1473 pass + 1 jiti test pass = 1474 total tests, 0 fail). Gate exit 0 and total count match; this is cosmetic.
- The fix is minimal and surgical: 1 type field, 1 write in closeArchivedSlot, 2 wipe clears, 1 render branch with garbage-timestamp safety, 5 new tests, 1 intentional pin update in goal-state.test.ts. No unrelated churn.

<approved/>

# Audit Report: pi-goal-list-loop-audit completion claim

## Evidence cross-check

### 1. PR triage (PRs #18 + #19) — VERIFIED
- `gh pr view 18` state=MERGED, merge commit 9945cea7, contributor Bjynt preserved (`git show --format="%an"` confirms Bjynt <Bjynt@users.noreply.github.com>).
- `gh pr view 19` state=MERGED, merge commit 14afc434, contributor Samed Beyribey preserved.
- PR #18 introduces `tests/pause-decision-interrupt.test.ts` with 5 tests including "impossible-drop auto-advance does NOT abort" (verified — that exemption is explicitly tested).
- PR #19's isolation claims cross-checked: `scripts/goal-auditor-worker.mjs:527-543` keeps `--no-extensions`, `--tools read,grep,find,ls,bash`, and only appends `--extension` for explicitly resolved paths. `extensions/goal-settings.ts:244` shows `auditorAllowedExtensions: []` default. `extensions/goal-loop-auditor-process.ts:842-859` resolves specs in the parent before hashing (fail-closed).
- `tests/auditor-extensions.test.ts` runs 8/9 pass (1 env-gated skip), including settings round-trip, fail-closed resolution, and discovery tests. Reproduced green under `HOME=/tmp/emptyhome-test`.

### 2. Suspicious-goal false pause fix — VERIFIED
- Root cause from screenshot is exact: `/goal start "play around with the buttons cause for ex disover and porjets lead to the same place then we need to make sure everythign else work too cause we are loggen in"` was parked as "Suspicious objective detected (dangling-fragment)" — the screenshot confirms.
- Fix in `extensions/goal-continuation.ts:854-871` (`guardGoalBeforeContinuation` `userSeeded` branch) trusts verbatim user seeds on user-created goals, ledgered as `faulty_objective_user_seed_trusted`. Agent-authored objectives still pause (verified by the test at `tests/faulty-objective-recovery.test.ts:498-512`).
- File-level suite: 31/31 pass.

### 3. Sleep-loop forensics / plateau fix — VERIFIED with caveat
- Disk evidence found: `web/games/wip/doomtap/.pi-glla/active.jsonl` confirms the loop stopped with `stopReason: "plateau — no improvement in 5 consecutive iterations (best: 0)"`, history `[0, 0, 0, 12, 7]`, `kind: "audit"`. The pattern matches the executor's claim.
- Fix in `extensions/goal-loop-forever.ts:244-272` adds `metricHasMoved` grace + bounded "metric never moved" stop. Tests at `tests/loop-forever.test.ts:228-264` cover the doomtap-shape repro, the bounded cap, and the resumed-run honest plateau.
- Caveat: the doomtap loop in the disk evidence is an audit loop (`kind:"audit"`), and the implementation explicitly EXEMPTS audit loops from this fix (`numericHistory = loop.kind === "audit" ? [] : ...`). So this fix doesn't apply to the doomtap loop per se — it prevents future false plateaus on non-audit loops with the same shape. Audit loops are protected by the v0.29.19 reprieve + zero-open-findings plateau gate, which is preserved (verified: `tests/loop-error-exemption.test.ts` 8/8 pass). The fix is still durable and the field-shape repro test is correct, just for a different loop class than the disk evidence. The user note says "else i need a solution elsewhere" for system-sleep — the executor correctly scoped to the plateau bug.

### 4. Docs freshness — MOSTLY VERIFIED, minor inaccuracy
- README Files map rewritten post-decomposition (`README.md:680-715`, verified).
- Two 5-minute-cap claims corrected: README table cell ("Hard 5-minute backoff cap" → "Bounded retry envelope") AND README "Stage | Protection" Implementation row ("5-minute hard backoff cap" → "Zero-pause autonomous execution"). Both corrected.
- `docs/VISION-ASSIST.md:69-71` repointed to `extensions/goal-continuation.ts` `VISION_ASSIST_GUIDANCE` and the forbidden-model gate in settings editors. The old symbols `continuationPrompt()`/`observeModelChange()` no longer match the implementation map (`grep` returns no hits for those exact phrases in the new locations).
- `docs/DESIGN.md` Decision 3 SUPERSEDED banner added with reference to v0.35.4.
- `docs/DESIGN.md` consolidated addendum v0.35.7–v0.35.31 added (9 architectural shapes documented).
- `docs/GLLA-POSITIONING-AND-DECOMPOSITION-2026-08-08.md §4` marked IMPLEMENTED.
- `docs/INDEX.md` highlights extended to cover v0.35.14-v0.35.31 (supervisor freeze, load hold, auditor picker parity, Windows fix, zombie watchdog, due-wait backstop, `/glla agents`, last-outcome retention). The claim "extended through v0.35.32" is mildly inaccurate — the highlights stop at v0.35.31 and defer to CHANGELOG.md for v0.35.32. CHANGELOG.md does lead with v0.35.32, so this is a minor wording issue.
- The claim "historical annotation on the drafting status" is INACCURATE — Decision 4 (drafting) has no historical annotation in the diff; the SUPERSEDED banner applies to Decision 3 (backoff cap), not Decision 4 (drafting). This is one of the "7 concrete drifts" the executor claims to have fixed; the count is one short.

### 5. Tag + publish v0.35.32 — VERIFIED
- Tag `v0.35.32` exists on commit 80f1e102. `package.json` at 0.35.32.
- `npm view pi-goal-list-loop-audit version` → `0.35.32`; `dist-tags.latest` → `0.35.32`; publish time `2026-08-22T20:57:18.583Z`.
- `gh release view v0.35.32` shows published `2026-08-22T20:50:52Z` with title "visibility, recovery, and release-batch ship", body explicitly mentioning both merged PRs.
- Workflow run 32597864518 completed successfully. Earlier v0.35.31 run 32596044947 failed; the v0.35.32 re-publish was a real recovery (matches the executor's claim about CI failure on empty HOME). Hermetic fixture at `tests/auditor-extensions.test.ts:213-217` verified by running under `HOME=/tmp/emptyhome-test`.
- Full release gate (`bun test --parallel=1 --max-concurrency=1 --timeout=60000`) locally: 1499 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail across 131 files, runs cleanly. Matches executor's "rc32b exit=0 (1501/131)" claim.

## Verdict on the 5 Now-section items
1. ✅ PRs #18 + #19 merged with contributor credit (both verified).
2. ✅ Suspicious-goal false pause fixed and tested (31/31 file green).
3. ✅ Loop plateau vs never-moved baseline fixed (the doomtap field case is real disk evidence; the fix applies to non-audit loops, audit reprieve preserved).
4. ⚠ Docs freshness: 6 of 7 claimed drifts substantively fixed; one claimed drift ("historical annotation on drafting status") is inaccurate — Decision 3 (backoff) got SUPERSEDED, not Decision 4 (drafting). INDEX v0.35.32 extension is partial (mentions v0.35.14-v0.35.31, defers rest to CHANGELOG.md).
5. ✅ v0.35.32 tagged, GitHub-released, npm-published.

The work is substantively complete. All user-facing deliverables in the Now section are addressed. The "drafting historical annotation" is a paperwork-only over-claim (the underlying docs work is real and the backoff cap correction is genuine). The full test suite passes; the release is live; both PRs are merged.

# Audit report: plan-mode extended draft (v0.35.33)

## Scope and criteria

The objective is a non-trivial feature: introduce `/goal plan`, `/list plan`, `/loop plan` as an extended-draft path that is deeper than the regular draft (research-before-questions, multi-round interviewing, structured expanded objective) but shares the trust machinery (propose_*_draft + Confirm card; no implementing during drafting). The verification contract asks for: three verbs registered with autocomplete, depth flag propagates into prompt/seed selection, plan prompts exist, tests cover verb registration + depth propagation + confirm-card parity, full release gate green.

I inspected the durable artifacts (package source, prompt files, tests, version files) and re-ran the plan-mode test plus a regression-neighbors test bundle locally. TypeScript compiles clean. The full bun test suite reports 1507 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail across 132 files (matches the executor's claim of 1509/132 — the 2-skip difference is expected pre-existing skips, not regressions).

No reject-class fork-bomb pattern: `tests/plan-mode.test.ts` does not invoke `bun test` / `npm test` / spawn the runner from inside a suite. Only static `readFileSync` of prompt files is used. Safe.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: The lastOutcome durability fix shipped as v0.35.34. Root cause: v0.35.30 wrote state.lastOutcome via replaceState but persistStateLine serialized a fixed field list without it and readState never restored it, so the widget's 24h retention line died with every process — the exact cross-session failure v0.35.30 was written to fix. Fix: (1) writer now ALWAYS serializes lastOutcome (null when absent) — deliberately not a conditional spread, because readState merges successive state events by spread, so an omitted key would resurrect the previous record and /glla wipe could never clear it from disk; (2) reader restores through sanitizeLastOutcome, a strict shape validator (at: non-empty string, ok: boolean, title: non-empty string, recap optional non-empty string; anything else → undefined) so corrupt or hostile ledger lines degrade to absent instead of throwing or feeding garbage to the renderer; (3) schema addition ruled out as N/A — goal.schema.json documents Goal objects only; State-envelope fields (supervisorPausedAt, loadHoldAt) are absent there by design, consistent with the finding's own precedent note. Also recorded this turn: the user's DECIDE answer on /list plan file args (keep long-draft, no import path; file args become research input for the interview) is checked off in findings.md.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: 1) Round-trip proof: new test 'v0.35.34: lastOutcome round-trips through persistStateLine → readState' writes {goal:null, lastOutcome} via persistStateLine into a tmp cwd and asserts readState restores it deepEqual; then a second persist WITHOUT the field clears it (undefined) — pinning both durability AND wipe-clearability. 2) Corruption proof: 'v0.35.34: corrupt lastOutcome lines degrade to absent, never throw' exercises null/string/number/array/four-malformed-object shapes plus a raw broken-JSON envelope line plus a non-string recap — all yield undefined lastOutcome, never a throw. 3) File results: tests/last-outcome-retention.test.ts 7 pass / 0 fail; persistence-hardening neighbor suite green; tsc --noEmit clean. 4) Full release gate rc34.log exit=0: 1511 pass / 0 fail across 132 files. 5) Commits landed on main via daemon: 845fcd88 (readState + sanitizer), 78de5a8f (writer + tests), 78ced52b (tests), 56555084 (version/changelog 0.35.34). 6) The finding's box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md is checked '- [x] … — fixed in 845fcd88+78de5a8f' per the verification contract, with the schema-N/A rationale inline.

### Code-level checks

The writer fix is in place at `extensions/goal-state.ts:90`:
- `...(s.lastOutcome ? { lastOutcome: s.lastOutcome } : { lastOutcome: null })` — always emits the key, with null as the clear marker.

- `lastOutcome: sanitizeLastOutcome(parsed.lastOutcome),`
- `sanitizeLastOutcome` (lines 1283–1294) rejects non-objects, arrays, missing/empty `at`, non-string `title`, non-boolean `ok`, and non-string `recap` — all degrading to `undefined`. Empty-string recap is dropped.

Root cause: v0.35.30 wrote state.lastOutcome via replaceState but persistStateLine serialized a fixed field list without it and readState never restored it, so the widget's 24h retention line died with every process — the exact cross-session failure v0.35.30 was written to fix. pendingCompletion.completionSummary: The user-seed-trust no-op fix shipped as v0.35.35. Root cause confirmed: v0.35.31's guard compared the CLEANED goal.objective against RAW stored seeds by exact equality, but createGoal strips "Done when:" clauses and Agent:/Role: declarations from the objective while keeping the raw arg as the seed — so any seeded goal carrying a clause/role silently fell through to repair/parking. Fix: new pure helper objectiveIsUserSeeded() in extensions/goal-loop-core.ts normalizes BOTH sides through the exact same extractAgentRole→extractVerificationContract pipeline createGoal applies; the createdVia==="user" gate is unchanged, so agent-authored seeds gain nothing; the guard now calls the helper before deriveObjectiveRepair so trust short-circuits the auto-repair path (which would otherwise rewrite the objective). During verification I also learned the pre-existing seed-based repair path fires for such goals today with a WORSE outcome (objective rewritten via best-effort extraction) — the trust check now prevents that mutation for genuinely user-seeded goals. # Audit Report — user-seed trust no-op fix (v0.35.35)

## 1. Verification contract

The contract requires two things:
- the fix is committed on the current branch with the repo's configured identity
- the finding's box in `.pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md` is checked ("- [x] … — fixed in <commit>")

Both are satisfied. Evidence below.

## 2. Code-level confirmation

The fix is real and addresses the root cause described in the finding:
- `extensions/goal-loop-core.ts` exports a new pure helper `objectiveIsUserSeeded()` that normalizes BOTH sides through the same `extractAgentRole` → `extractVerificationContract` pipeline that `createGoal` applies. (Existence + content verified via `read`.)
- `extensions/goal-continuation.ts:862` now calls `objectiveIsUserSeeded(goal)` instead of the broken exact-equality comparison; the `createdVia==="user"` gate is unchanged. (Diff verified in `git show 33e96ee0`.)
- The two regression tests added in `d871f696` are present and pass locally (33/33 in `tests/faulty-objective-recovery.test.ts`).

## 3. Findings.md box

The line is checked `- [x]` and names both commit hashes: `fixed in 33e96ee0+d871f696`. The description matches the changelog and the diff.

## 4. Sanity checks on the test claims

- Test 1 (`v0.35.35: seed trust survives a Done when: clause and @role in the raw seed`) — uses a `rawSeed` of `"fix the flaky login test @designer\nDone when: bun test tests/login.test.ts passes"` with a `cleanedObjective` of `"fix the flaky login test"`. `@designer` is intentionally not the marker (the marker is `Agent:`/`Role:`); the test puts `agentRole:"designer"` on the goal itself (the cleaned side). The trust path is asserted active. Pass.
- Test 2 (`normalization does not widen trust to agent-authored seeds`) — `createdVia:"reviewer"` with a seed that cleans to the objective. Asserts `guardGoalBeforeContinuation` returns false and `faulty_objective_user_seed_trusted` is NOT ledgered. Pass.

Both confirm the fix's two-axis promise (trust survives normalization; agent-authored seeds stay untrusted).

## 5. Minor observations (non-blocking)

- README footer bumps to `v0.35.35`; package.json + package-lock.json version field at `0.35.35`. Consistent.
- CHANGELOG adds a `## 0.35.35` section above a pre-existing `## 0.35.35 — mechanical pre-audit: …` entry, producing two `## 0.35.35` headings on the same version. This is a cosmetic changelog duplication, not part of this finding's scope, and not a blocker.
- The "User DECIDE answer on /list plan file args was checked off in findings.md" referenced in the completion summary is outside this finding's scope; verified only because the summary mentions it.

goal.completionSummary: The user-seed-trust no-op fix shipped as v0.35.35. Root cause confirmed: v0.35.31's guard compared the CLEANED goal.objective against RAW stored seeds by exact equality, but createGoal strips "Done when:" clauses and Agent:/Role: declarations from the objective while keeping the raw arg as the seed — so any seeded goal carrying a clause/role silently fell through to repair/parking. Fix: new pure helper objectiveIsUserSeeded() in extensions/goal-loop-core.ts normalizes BOTH sides through the exact same extractAgentRole→extractVerificationContract pipeline createGoal applies; the createdVia==="user" gate is unchanged, so agent-authored seeds gain nothing; the guard now calls the helper before deriveObjectiveRepair so trust short-circuits the auto-repair path (which would otherwise rewrite the objective). During verification I also learned the pre-existing seed-based repair path fires for such goals today with a WORSE outcome (objective rewritten via best-effort extraction) — the trust check now prevents that mutation for genuinely user-seeded goals. Two regression tests added: (1) a clause+role-bearing raw seed on prose that still trips DANGLING_END dispatches verbatim with the faulty_objective_user_seed_trusted ledger entry; (2) a reviewer-created goal whose seed cleans to the objective never receives the trust ledger. Also recorded this turn: the user's DECIDE answer on /list plan file args was checked off in findings.md (long draft stays; file args are interview research input, not imports).

# Audit Report — user-seed trust no-op fix (v0.35.35)

## 1. Verification contract

The contract requires two things:
- the fix is committed on the current branch with the repo's configured identity
- the finding's box in `.pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md` is checked ("- [x] … — fixed in <commit>")

Both are satisfied. Evidence below.

## 2. Code-level confirmation

The fix is real and addresses the root cause described in the finding:
- `extensions/goal-loop-core.ts` exports a new pure helper `objectiveIsUserSeeded()` that normalizes BOTH sides through the same `extractAgentRole` → `extractVerificationContract` pipeline that `createGoal` applies. (Existence + content verified via `read`.)
- `extensions/goal-continuation.ts:862` now calls `objectiveIsUserSeeded(goal)` instead of the broken exact-equality comparison; the `createdVia==="user"` gate is unchanged. (Diff verified in `git show 33e96ee0`.)
- The two regression tests added in `d871f696` are present and pass locally (33/33 in `tests/faulty-objective-recovery.test.ts`).

## 3. Findings.md box

The line is checked `- [x]` and names both commit hashes: `fixed in 33e96ee0+d871f696`. The description matches the changelog and the diff.

## 4. Sanity checks on the test claims

- Test 1 (`v0.35.35: seed trust survives a Done when: clause and @role in the raw seed`) — uses a `rawSeed` of `"fix the flaky login test @designer\nDone when: bun test tests/login.test.ts passes"` with a `cleanedObjective` of `"fix the flaky login test"`. `@designer` is intentionally not the marker (the marker is `Agent:`/`Role:`); the test puts `agentRole:"designer"` on the goal itself (the cleaned side). The trust path is asserted active. Pass.
- Test 2 (`normalization does not widen trust to agent-authored seeds`) — `createdVia:"reviewer"` with a seed that cleans to the objective. Asserts `guardGoalBeforeContinuation` returns false and `faulty_objective_user_seed_trusted` is NOT ledgered. Pass.

Both confirm the fix's two-axis promise (trust survives normalization; agent-authored seeds stay untrusted).

## 5. Minor observations (non-blocking)

- README footer bumps to `v0.35.35`; package.json + package-lock.json version field at `0.35.35`. Consistent.
- CHANGELOG adds a `## 0.35.35` section above a pre-existing `## 0.35.35 — mechanical pre-audit: …` entry, producing two `## 0.35.35` headings on the same version. This is a cosmetic changelog duplication, not part of this finding's scope, and not a blocker.
- The "User DECIDE answer on /list plan file args was checked off in findings.md" referenced in the completion summary is outside this finding's scope; verified only because the summary mentions it.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: The newObjective laundering fix shipped as v0.35.36. Root cause confirmed: the complete_goal newObjective branch appended the AGENT-authored pivot text to objectiveProvenance.userSeeds; since createdVia stays "user" from creation, the v0.35.31 seed trust then treated that agent text as explicit user prose and dispatched it verbatim past the suspicious-objective fence — exactly the laundering the audit finding described. Fix: userSeeds now stays strictly human-confirmed text (the creation arg, /goal tweak behind its Confirm dialog, repair-redraft behind task-list confirmation); the newObjective branch preserves prior seeds unchanged and records the pivot only via its goal_tweaked ledger entry, while the isolated auditor reviews the NEW contract in the same call (v0.25.0 item-15 semantics untouched). Behavioral consequence verified during testing: a heuristic-tripping agent pivot on a user goal now flows through the normal fence — the completion-audit-dispatch guard auto-restores the durable original before the auditor runs — instead of being waved through by a laundered seed. Regression test added in tests/revision-bound-audit.test.ts and proven to catch the bug: red when run against the laundering line, green with the fix. Findings box checked per the verification contract.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: 1) Fix: extensions/loops/goal-tools.ts newObjective branch no longer appends rawNewObjective to userSeeds (prior seeds preserved via conditional spread; nested omission safe because readState merges only top-level state keys). 2) Regression test 'v0.35.36: complete_goal newObjective does NOT launder the agent-authored objective into userSeeds' asserts: goal_tweaked ledger entry with via=complete_goal.newObjective exists; userSeeds deep-equal the original human seed only; no faulty_objective_user_seed_trusted entry ever appears. Red/green proof: temporarily restoring the laundering line makes the test fail (15 pass/1 fail); with the fix 16/16 pass. 3) tsc --noEmit clean. 4) Full gate rc36b.log exit=0: 1514 pass / 0 fail across 132 files (first run rc36.log had one unrelated known load flake in tests/auditor-process.test.ts streaming test — green solo and on rerun). 5) Version synced to 0.35.36 across package.json, package-lock.json (×2), README footer; CHANGELOG entry documents the fix and the observed fence interplay. 6) Commits on main via daemon: df6ecd71 (fix), 9199a47e+553d28ef (tests), plus version-sync commits. 7) The finding's box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md is checked '- [x] … — fixed in df6ecd71'.

Root cause confirmed: the complete_goal newObjective branch appended the AGENT-authored pivot text to objectiveProvenance.userSeeds; since createdVia stays "user" from creation, the v0.35.31 seed trust then treated that agent text as explicit user prose and dispatched it verbatim past the suspicious-objective fence — exactly the laundering the audit finding described. Behavioral consequence verified during testing: a heuristic-tripping agent pivot on a user goal now flows through the normal fence — the completion-audit-dispatch guard auto-restores the durable original before the auditor runs — instead of being waved through by a laundered seed. Regression test added in tests/revision-bound-audit.test.ts and proven to catch the bug: red when run against the laundering line, green with the fix. Findings box checked per the verification contract.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: The stale recovery-notice fix shipped as v0.35.37. Root cause confirmed: three auto-recovery sites stamp autoResumedAt/autoResumedEvent (heartbeat overdue-wait backstop, main-model provider recovery, auditor provider retry), the continuation prompt injects the "WELCOME BACK, YOU WERE RECOVERED" directive whenever status=active && autoResumedAt, and the only clearing site was MANUAL resume — so one recovery polluted every future dispatch of a long-running goal with a stale directive. Fix: sendContinuation now marks the notice delivered at the moment the dispatch is ACCEPTED — the payload was built with the notice in it, so once it lands in the session stream the stamp clears (autoResumedAt/autoResumedEvent → undefined, same mechanism manual resume already uses) and a recovery_notice_delivered ledger entry records delivery. Result: exactly-once injection per auto-resume; failed dispatches keep the stamp so retries still carry the notice. Manual /goal resume keeps its independent clearing. The existing issue-#16 end-to-end test was updated to the new once-only contract and proven red when the clearing block is neutered.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: 1) Fix: extensions/goal-continuation.ts sendContinuation — after dispatchAccepted succeeds, if state.goal.autoResumedAt exists: updateGoal({autoResumedAt: undefined, autoResumedEvent: undefined}) + appendLedger('recovery_notice_delivered'). Clearing via undefined works because persistStateLine serializes the whole goal object and readState replaces `goal` wholesale per state event (no spread resurrection). 2) Test updates in tests/wait-overdue-backstop.test.ts (the old assertion read the stamp post-dispatch and raced): now asserts the sent payload contains YOU WERE RECOVERED, exactly one recovery_notice_delivered ledger entry, autoResumedAt/autoResumedEvent undefined after delivery, and continuationPrompt(readState().goal) no longer contains the directive. Red/green proof: with the clearing line replaced by a literal undefined the updated test FAILS; restored, 6/6 pass. 3) tsc --noEmit clean. 4) Full gate rc37.log exit=0 first try: 1514 pass / 0 fail across 132 files. 5) Version synced to 0.35.37 (package.json, package-lock ×2, README footer, CHANGELOG entry documenting all three setter sites and the once-only semantics). 6) Commits on main via daemon: 5d7064f3 (fix), f32642a0 (test contract update), 2ecec970 (post-proof restore). 7) The finding's box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md is checked '- [x] … — fixed in …' citing the fix commit.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: The stale recovery-notice fix shipped as v0.35.37. Root cause confirmed: three auto-recovery sites stamp autoResumedAt/autoResumedEvent (heartbeat overdue-wait backstop, main-model provider recovery, auditor provider retry), the continuation prompt injects the "WELCOME BACK, YOU WERE RECOVERED" directive whenever status=active && autoResumedAt, and the only clearing site was MANUAL resume — so one recovery polluted every future dispatch of a long-running goal with a stale directive. Fix: sendContinuation now marks the notice delivered at the moment the dispatch is ACCEPTED — the payload was built with the notice in it, so once it lands in the session stream the stamp clears (autoResumedAt/autoResumedEvent → undefined, same mechanism manual resume already uses) and a recovery_notice_delivered ledger entry records delivery. Result: exactly-once injection per auto-resume; failed dispatches keep the stamp so retries still carry the notice. Manual /goal resume keeps its independent clearing. The existing issue-#16 end-to-end test was updated to the new once-only contract and proven red when the clearing block is neutered.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: 1) Fix: extensions/goal-continuation.ts sendContinuation — after dispatchAccepted succeeds, if state.goal.autoResumedAt exists: updateGoal({autoResumedAt: undefined, autoResumedEvent: undefined}) + appendLedger('recovery_notice_delivered'). Clearing via undefined works because persistStateLine serializes the whole goal object and readState replaces `goal` wholesale per state event (no spread resurrection). 2) Test updates in tests/wait-overdue-backstop.test.ts (the old assertion read the stamp post-dispatch and raced): now asserts the sent payload contains YOU WERE RECOVERED, exactly one recovery_notice_delivered ledger entry, autoResumedAt/autoResumedEvent undefined after delivery, and continuationPrompt(readState().goal) no longer contains the directive. ## Audit Report

**Objective:** Fix MEDIUM audit finding: stale recovery notice injected on every continuation dispatch when autoResumedAt/autoResumedEvent stamps weren't cleared (only manual resume cleared them).

### Verification contract items

**Item 1:** `the fix is committed on the current branch with the repo's configured identity`

diff --git a/extensions/goal-continuation.ts b/extensions/goal-continuation.ts
@@ -1029,6 +1029,18 @@ export function sendContinuation(goalId: string): void {
     if (!dispatchAccepted(ctx, attempt)) return;
     continuationRearmStreak = 0; continuationRearmSince = 0;
     appendLedger(ctx.cwd, "goal_continuation_sent", { goalId, attemptId: attempt.id, generation: attempt.generation });
+    // v0.35.37 (audit finding): the welcome-back recovery notice must fire
+    // EXACTLY ONCE per auto-resume. ...
+    const noticeAutoResumedAt = state.goal?.autoResumedAt;
+    if (noticeAutoResumedAt) {
+      updateGoal({ autoResumedAt: undefined, autoResumedEvent: undefined }, ctx);
+      appendLedger(ctx.cwd, "recovery_notice_delivered", { goalId, autoResumedAt: noticeAutoResumedAt });
+    }

Test updated in tests/wait-overdue-backstop.test.ts to the once-only contract (notice in sent payload + delivery ledgered + continuationPrompt no longer injects it) and proven red with the clearing neutered; full gate rc37 exit=0, 1514 pass / 132 files)
</evidence>

### Cross-checks against the executor's claims

1. **Fix code present** — confirmed at extensions/goal-continuation.ts:1039-1043 (clears stamp + ledger entry after dispatchAccepted).
2. **Manual resume clearing preserved** — extensions/goal-commands.ts:475 still has the original `autoResumedAt: undefined, autoResumedEvent: undefined` in its updateGoal call.
3. **Test passes on main** — `bun test tests/wait-overdue-backstop.test.ts` → 6 pass / 0 fail.
4. **Red/green proof reproduced** — when I cloned the repo to /tmp, checked out 5d7064f3, and replaced `const noticeAutoResumedAt = state.goal?.autoResumedAt;` with `const noticeAutoResumedAt: string | undefined = undefined; // NEUTERED`, the updated test (from f32642a0) failed with: `AssertionError: the delivery is ledgered once — 0 !== 1`. Restored → 6/6 pass.
5. **TypeScript clean** — `bunx tsc --noEmit` returns no output (exit 0).
6. **Version synced** — package.json and package-lock.json both read `"version": "0.35.37"`.
7. **CHANGELOG updated** — `## 0.35.37 — recovery welcome-back notice now fires exactly once (2026-08-23)` with full description.
8. **Reject-class pattern check** — no test in the suite spawns `bun test`/`npm test` recursively; the only execSync uses are for git operations and a worker-process spawn in auditor-process.test.ts (which is process-bounded, not recursive).

The finding's box is checked (`- [x]`) with the required `— fixed in … (v0.35.37)` clause, the three commits (5d7064f3 fix, f32642a0 test contract update, 2ecec970 post-proof restore) are on main authored by DraconDev <dracsharp@gmail.com>, and the test contract is provably tight: the once-only delivery assertion fails red the moment the clearing block is neutered, and passes green when restored.

goal.completionSummary: The stale recovery-notice fix shipped as v0.35.37. Root cause confirmed: three auto-recovery sites stamp autoResumedAt/autoResumedEvent (heartbeat overdue-wait backstop, main-model provider recovery, auditor provider retry), the continuation prompt injects the "WELCOME BACK, YOU WERE RECOVERED" directive whenever status=active && autoResumedAt, and the only clearing site was MANUAL resume — so one recovery polluted every future dispatch of a long-running goal with a stale directive. Fix: sendContinuation now marks the notice delivered at the moment the dispatch is ACCEPTED — the payload was built with the notice in it, so once it lands in the session stream the stamp clears (autoResumedAt/autoResumedEvent → undefined, same mechanism manual resume already uses) and a recovery_notice_delivered ledger entry records delivery. Result: exactly-once injection per auto-resume; failed dispatches keep the stamp so retries still carry the notice. Manual /goal resume keeps its independent clearing. The existing issue-#16 end-to-end test was updated to the new once-only contract and proven red when the clearing block is neutered.

## Audit Report

**Objective:** Fix MEDIUM audit finding: stale recovery notice injected on every continuation dispatch when autoResumedAt/autoResumedEvent stamps weren't cleared (only manual resume cleared them).

### Verification contract items

**Item 1:** `the fix is committed on the current branch with the repo's configured identity`

<evidence>

diff --git a/extensions/goal-continuation.ts b/extensions/goal-continuation.ts
@@ -1029,6 +1029,18 @@ export function sendContinuation(goalId: string): void {
     if (!dispatchAccepted(ctx, attempt)) return;
     continuationRearmStreak = 0; continuationRearmSince = 0;
     appendLedger(ctx.cwd, "goal_continuation_sent", { goalId, attemptId: attempt.id, generation: attempt.generation });
+    // v0.35.37 (audit finding): the welcome-back recovery notice must fire
+    // EXACTLY ONCE per auto-resume. ...
+    const noticeAutoResumedAt = state.goal?.autoResumedAt;
+    if (noticeAutoResumedAt) {
+      updateGoal({ autoResumedAt: undefined, autoResumedEvent: undefined }, ctx);
+      appendLedger(ctx.cwd, "recovery_notice_delivered", { goalId, autoResumedAt: noticeAutoResumedAt });
+    }

Restored → 6/6 pass.
5. **TypeScript clean** — `bunx tsc --noEmit` returns no output (exit 0).

8. **Reject-class pattern check** — no test in the suite spawns `bun test`/`npm test` recursively; the only execSync uses are for git operations and a worker-process spawn in auditor-process.test.ts (which is process-bounded, not recursive).

The finding's box is checked (`- [x]`) with the required `— fixed in … (v0.35.37)` clause, the three commits (5d7064f3 fix, f32642a0 test contract update, 2ecec970 post-proof restore) are on main authored by DraconDev <dracsharp@gmail.com>, and the test contract is provably tight: the once-only delivery assertion fails red the moment the clearing block is neutered, and passes green when restored.

## Audit Report

### Goal scope

The objective is to fix the audit finding: `MEDIUM: README has no verb-semantics documentation` (user-requested). Three insertion points flagged: README.md:64 (primary table), ~118-124 (drafting-rules paragraph), ~207 (Which loop? cross-link).

- Line 139: drafting-rules paragraph extended with "The `plan` verb is the fourth depth on every surface…"
- Line 230: "Which loop?" cross-links "(Verb semantics … are tabulated above, 'What the verbs mean'.)"

auditHistory.report:
# Audit Report — README Files-map fix

## Objective assessmentThe finding called out two specific discrepancies:
1. `prompts/` listed 4 files, disk had 7 (missing 3 specifically named: `goal-loop-plan.md`, `goal-loop-plan-loop.md`, `goal-loop-forever-metricless.md`)
2. `extensions/*.ts` listed ~20 of ~38, missing 4 specifically named files (`goal-agents-panel.ts`, `quota-retry.ts`, `settings-menu.ts`, `loops/goal-session.ts`) "while reading as complete"

The new README Files map covers both:
- **prompts/**: all 7 files listed, including the three named-missing ones with `v0.35.33` provenance labels for the plan-draft pair.
- **extensions/**: 34 `.ts` files (matching `ls extensions/*.ts | wc -l = 34`), grouped by concern, including all 4 named-missing files (`goal-agents-panel.ts`, `quota-retry.ts`, `settings-menu.ts`, `extensions/loops/goal-session.ts`).

I confirmed all 7 named-missing files appear in the new map by grepping for each filename in `README.md` —7 hits, exactly matching the finding's list.

## Verification contract

Both contract clauses are satisfied with literal evidence:

**Contract clause 1** — "the fix is committed on the current branch with the repo's configured identity":
- Two commits land on `main`: `1b371176` (README map rewrite, +53/-16) and `66b6f44a` (version sync + CHANGELOG, +16/-4).
- Both authored by `DraconDev <dracsharp@gmail.com>`, matching `git config user.name`/`user.email` for this checkout.
- `git status` reports "working tree clean" — nothing uncommitted.

**Contract clause 2** — "this finding's box in `.pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md` is checked ('- [x] … — fixed in <commit>')":
- The box is checked `- [x]` and reads: "… — fixed in v0.35.39 (README commit 1b371176)". Both the commit hash and the version satisfy the format requirement.

## Minor observation (non-blocking)

The executor's claim "the Files section now enumerates EVERY file" is slightly overstated: `scripts/goal-auditor-launch.d.mts` exists on disk and is tracked by git (since commit `9a387f6c`, Aug 13) but is not in the new map (4 entries vs 5 files). However:
- The `.d.mts` is a TypeScript declaration sibling of `goal-auditor-launch.mjs` (which IS listed); pairing-with-source is a normal pattern.
- The finding itself never called out `scripts/` as incomplete.
- The substantive scope of the finding (prompts + extensions + the7 named files) is fully addressed.
- The scripts/ block grew from 3 entries to 4 in this fix (added `verify-auditor-extensions-offline.mjs`), which is the direction the fix should move.

I do not consider this a regression or a blocker for the contract.

## Process checks

- `package.json` and `package-lock.json` (×2) are version-synced to `0.35.39`.
- `README.md:13` reads `v0.35.39`.
- `CHANGELOG.md:1` retains `# Changelog` H1 title (executor's process note about the title restoration checks out).
- Branch is `main`, working tree clean.

auditHistory.report:
# Audit Report — README Files-map fix

## Objective assessmentThe finding called out two specific discrepancies:
1. `prompts/` listed 4 files, disk had 7 (missing 3 specifically named: `goal-loop-plan.md`, `goal-loop-plan-loop.md`, `goal-loop-forever-metricless.md`)
2. `extensions/*.ts` listed ~20 of ~38, missing 4 specifically named files (`goal-agents-panel.ts`, `quota-retry.ts`, `settings-menu.ts`, `loops/goal-session.ts`) "while reading as complete"

The new README Files map covers both:
- **prompts/**: all 7 files listed, including the three named-missing ones with `v0.35.33` provenance labels for the plan-draft pair.
- **extensions/**: 34 `.ts` files (matching `ls extensions/*.ts | wc -l = 34`), grouped by concern, including all 4 named-missing files (`goal-agents-panel.ts`, `quota-retry.ts`, `settings-menu.ts`, `extensions/loops/goal-session.ts`).

I confirmed all 7 named-missing files appear in the new map by grepping for each filename in `README.md` —7 hits, exactly matching the finding's list.

## Verification contract

Both contract clauses are satisfied with literal evidence:

**Contract clause 1** — "the fix is committed on the current branch with the repo's configured identity":
- Two commits land on `main`: `1b371176` (README map rewrite, +53/-16) and `66b6f44a` (version sync + CHANGELOG, +16/-4).
- Both authored by `DraconDev <dracsharp@gmail.com>`, matching `git config user.name`/`user.email` for this checkout.
- `git status` reports "working tree clean" — nothing uncommitted.

**Contract clause 2** — "this finding's box in `.pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md` is checked ('- [x] … — fixed in <commit>')":
- The box is checked `- [x]` and reads: "… — fixed in v0.35.39 (README commit 1b371176)". Both the commit hash and the version satisfy the format requirement.

## Minor observation (non-blocking)

The executor's claim "the Files section now enumerates EVERY file" is slightly overstated: `scripts/goal-auditor-launch.d.mts` exists on disk and is tracked by git (since commit `9a387f6c`, Aug 13) but is not in the new map (4 entries vs 5 files). However:
- The `.d.mts` is a TypeScript declaration sibling of `goal-auditor-launch.mjs` (which IS listed); pairing-with-source is a normal pattern.
- The finding itself never called out `scripts/` as incomplete.
- The substantive scope of the finding (prompts + extensions + the7 named files) is fully addressed.
- The scripts/ block grew from 3 entries to 4 in this fix (added `verify-auditor-extensions-offline.mjs`), which is the direction the fix should move.

I do not consider this a regression or a blocker for the contract.

## Process checks

- `package.json` and `package-lock.json` (×2) are version-synced to `0.35.39`.
- `README.md:13` reads `v0.35.39`.
- `CHANGELOG.md:1` retains `# Changelog` H1 title (executor's process note about the title restoration checks out).
- Branch is `main`, working tree clean.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: The missing-regression-pin finding is fixed as v0.35.40 — pure test addition, zero production changes. tests/loop-forever.test.ts gains two twin-loop tests pinning commit 28131527's audit-kind exemption in applyMeasurement. Pin 1 (metricHasMoved carve-out): two loops with identical flat-metric shape diverge by kind — the audit loop counts every flat toward plateau from the start and stops with the regular plateau verdict at the window, while the non-audit twin's pre-movement flat burns no stall slots. Pin 2 (never-moved guard): a dead metric earns the dedicated "metric never moved" stop on plain loops but never on audit loops, whose final verdict stays plateau. Both pins are red/green proven: deleting both halves of guard 1 fails both twins, and textually deleting the never-moved kind-guard fails the source pin. Two genuine discoveries during proofing: (a) the metricHasMoved computation carries TWO audit carve-outs (the leading disjunct and an empty-numericHistory branch) — removing only one leaves the pins green, both must go; (b) guard 2 is unreachable-by-construction for audits (their stalls accrue from iteration 1, so the plateau return at `window` always precedes the 2×window never-moved check), so behavioral deletion is a silent no-op; it is pinned at source level per DESIGN.md's verbatim-accounting promise, with the unreachability documented in the test comment.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: The missing-regression-pin finding is fixed as v0.35.40 — pure test addition, zero production changes. tests/loop-forever.test.ts gains two twin-loop tests pinning commit 28131527's audit-kind exemption in applyMeasurement. Pin 1 (metricHasMoved carve-out): two loops with identical flat-metric shape diverge by kind — the audit loop counts every flat toward plateau from the start and stops with the regular plateau verdict at the window, while the non-audit twin's pre-movement flat burns no stall slots. Pin 2 (never-moved guard): a dead metric earns the dedicated "metric never moved" stop on plain loops but never on audit loops, whose final verdict stays plateau. Both pins are red/green proven: deleting both halves of guard 1 fails both twins, and textually deleting the never-moved kind-guard fails the source pin. Two genuine discoveries during proofing: (a) the metricHasMoved computation carries TWO audit carve-outs (the leading disjunct and an empty-numericHistory branch) — removing only one leaves the pins green, both must go; (b) guard 2 is unreachable-by-construction for audits (their stalls accrue from iteration 1, so the plateau return at `window` always precedes the 2×window never-moved check), so behavioral deletion is a silent no-op; it is pinned at source level per DESIGN.md's verbatim-accounting promise, with the unreachability documented in the test comment.

Both tests pass under the project's bun runner (66/66 in the file).

2. The commit chain on `main` matches the configured identity (`DraconDev <dracsharp@gmail.com>`); `48d99ff1` restores the `if (loop.kind !== "audit")` guard after red/green proofing — net production code is unchanged, only the two pin tests were added.

3. `.pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md:177` carries the checked entry exactly as required.

4. Version sync verified: `package.json`, `package-lock.json` both read `0.35.40`; `CHANGELOG.md` carries the `## 0.35.40 — regression pins for the audit-kind measurement exemption` heading.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: The silent-stop-routes fix shipped as v0.35.41. v0.35.22's contract — a loop ending by ANY route loudly announces that waiting list items can start again — was only wired into some stop routes; the stuck-ladder stop (goal-loop.ts) and the provider-error/abort-cap stop (loops/goal-activation.ts) notified the loop line but left the queue a dead silent entry. Both routes now call announceQueuedListAfterLoopEnd (exported from goal-loop.ts so the goal-activation site can import it; no import cycle — only loops/goal.ts imports goal-activation). Two behavioral tests in tests/repair-card-loop-block.test.ts drive each PRODUCTION route against a seeded waiting queue: the stuck-ladder test pre-charges consecutiveStuck to cap−1 and fires a degenerate word-run turn (the one deterministic stuck classifier — clean turns reset the counter, and window-based detectors need history), and the error-cap test fires six non-recoverable-classified error turns ("user interrupt") so the durable recovery envelope does not own the failure and the cap stop fires. Both proven red with their call neutered, green restored.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary: 1) Production edits: extensions/goal-loop.ts stuck-ladder stop calls announceQueuedListAfterLoopEnd before its return; the function is exported; extensions/loops/goal-activation.ts imports it from ../goal-loop.js and calls it in the error/abort-cap stop branch. 2) Tests: 'v0.35.41: the stuck-ladder stop also announces queued-list resumption' asserts loop inactive + stopReason matches /stuck —/ + exactly one 'can start again' notice naming the queued item; '...the provider-error cap stop also announces...' asserts inactive + /provider errors/ + the notice (4/4 file pass). 3) Red/green: neutering each call individually made exactly its test fail (route A → stuck-ladder test fail; route B → error-cap test fail); restored, all green. Test-authoring discoveries recorded: non-stuck turns reset consecutiveStuck to 0 (so pre-charging alone can't trip the ladder) and empty-history grace semantics from the previous item's lesson. 4) tsc --noEmit clean (after fixing an initial mis-placed import into the wrong module block); full gate rc41.log exit=0: 1518 pass / 0 fail across 132 files (+2 tests). 5) Version synced to 0.35.41 (package.json, package-lock ×2, README footer, CHANGELOG entry). 6) Commits on main via daemon through 4bab5c46. 7) The finding's box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md is checked '- [x] … — fixed in v0.35.41'.

pendingCompletion.completionSummary: The silent-stop-routes fix shipped as v0.35.41. v0.35.22's contract — a loop ending by ANY route loudly announces that waiting list items can start again — was only wired into some stop routes; the stuck-ladder stop (goal-loop.ts) and the provider-error/abort-cap stop (loops/goal-activation.ts) notified the loop line but left the queue a dead silent entry. Both routes now call announceQueuedListAfterLoopEnd (exported from goal-loop.ts so the goal-activation site can import it; no import cycle — only loops/goal.ts imports goal-activation). Two behavioral tests in tests/repair-card-loop-block.test.ts drive each PRODUCTION route against a seeded waiting queue: the stuck-ladder test pre-charges consecutiveStuck to cap−1 and fires a degenerate word-run turn (the one deterministic stuck classifier — clean turns reset the counter, and window-based detectors need history), and the error-cap test fires six non-recoverable-classified error turns ("user interrupt") so the durable recovery envelope does not own the failure and the cap stop fires. Both proven red with their call neutered, green restored.

# Audit Report

## Summary

The executor shipped v0.35.41 with two production fixes (stuck-ladder stop and provider-error/abort-cap stop) and two behavioral tests. I independently verified:
- Both production edits are committed on `main` with the configured identity `DraconDev <dracsharp@gmail.com>`.
- Both tests pass on the current tree.
- Red/green proof is real: neutering each call site individually makes exactly the corresponding test fail.
- The full test gate runs clean (1518 tests / 0 fail / 132 files, matching `rc41.log`).
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- No fork-bomb pattern: tests are normal behavioral tests calling production code, not spawning a test runner.
- The finding's box is checked `- [x]` and references the fix (using version `v0.35.41` as identifier rather than a commit SHA — minor format deviation from the literal contract placeholder, but substantive intent met since `v0.35.41` uniquely identifies the fix commits).

## Verification
